title: Light's Criteria (Pleural Effusion)
keywords: ANY one criterion positive means exudate
pleural LDH over two-thirds ULN serum LDH
misclassifies 25-30 percent of heart-failure transudates as exudate — use albumin gradient if suspicious
sources: Light RW, et al. Pleural effusions: the diagnostic separation of transudates and exudates. Ann Intern Med. 1972;77(4):507-513 (original criteria).

changelog.change: Initial entry — a genuine content gap (Content audit 2026-09-14, Batch 3). Built as an additive checklist (any-one-positive = exudate) rather than a threshold score — Light's Criteria is a rule-out-transudate decision rule, not a summed score, so the additive engine is reused for that any-one-positive logic exactly as preeclampsia-severe-features was in Batch 2.
Reformatted for reading on a phone: long paragraphs broken into short paragraphs and lists. Wording and clinical content unchanged.

purpose: Distinguish exudative from transudative pleural effusion at the bedside — an effusion is exudative if it meets ANY ONE of the three criteria below.
notes:
This is a rule-out-transudate decision rule, not a point-threshold score: ANY single criterion being positive classifies the effusion as exudative, so the 'score' here is really a count of how many of the 3 criteria are met (0 = transudate, 1-3 = exudate — the count above 0 doesn't change the classification, only confirms it more ways).

Light's Criteria over-calls exudate in roughly 25-30% of heart-failure-related transudates, usually after diuresis has concentrated the protein/LDH. If the clinical picture screams heart failure but Light's says exudate, check rather than overriding on gestalt alone:
- a serum-to-pleural albumin gradient (> 1.2 g/dL favors transudate)
- or protein gradient (> 3.1 g/dL favors transudate)

items.label: Pleural fluid protein / serum protein ratio > 0.5
Pleural fluid LDH / serum LDH ratio > 0.6
Pleural fluid LDH > 2/3 of the upper limit of normal for serum LDH

interpretation.label: Transudate
interpretation.detail: No criterion met. Think heart failure, cirrhosis/hepatic hydrothorax, nephrotic syndrome, or hypoalbuminemia — manage the underlying systemic process, not the pleural space itself.

interpretation.label: Exudate
interpretation.detail: One or more criteria met. Send further pleural fluid studies (cell count/differential, glucose, pH, cytology, culture ± cholesterol/triglycerides if chylothorax suspected) to work toward the specific cause — parapneumonic/empyema, malignancy, PE, TB, and many others.
